clue.text: Happen support for horse will lead to benefit

parts.note: to happen is to be, as in 'so be it'
a horse stands on its hooves, so a hoof supports it

explanation.surface: A bettor hopes that backing a horse will pay off.
explanation.definitionFit: Behoof is an old word for advantage or profit, as in 'for his behoof'.

clue.text: Rebound in success with line of goods having latest item promoted

parts.note: a boom is a period of great success

indicators.note: promoted in a down clue means moved up, so the last letter goes to the front

parts.note: a range is a line of products

explanation.surface: A firm's success bounces back after its newest product is pushed.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the final E of RANGE to the front gives ERANG.
explanation.definitionFit: To boomerang is to recoil on the person who started it, to rebound.

clue.text: Hard to supplant working NASA center

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to oust is to drive out and take the place of, to supplant
on means working, as a switched-on machine is

explanation.surface: Someone tough plans to take over a working space centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard to supplant' reads as one phrase about difficulty but splits into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Johnson Space Center, mission control for crewed flights, is in Houston, Texas.

clue.text: Ocean rover at sea holding it up in extreme response

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece goes inside the other
at sea means confused, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the letters go backwards

explanation.surface: A vessel exploring the ocean is held up and someone panics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges the letters of OCEAN ROVER, and 'up' turns the clue's 'it' over before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An overreaction is a response out of proportion to its cause, too extreme.

clue.text: Brawl sees American in American gorge retreating

indicators.note: something retreating goes back, so the built word is read backwards
the American is placed inside the gorge word

parts.note: to scarf is American slang for to gorge, eat greedily

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out with an American caught in a canyon somewhere in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' looks like a canyon but is the verb to eat greedily. Putting A inside SCARF gives SACARF, which 'retreating' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy disturbance or scuffle, a synonym of brawl.

clue.text: Scoundrel capturing Conservative wearing the special gear?

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person, a scoundrel

indicators.note: the Conservative wears the word the around it, so C goes inside

explanation.surface: A villain grabs a Tory who's dressed in some special kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts C within the clue's 'the' to give TCHE; the question mark admits 'special gear' is a loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet is a toothed wheel with a pawl letting it turn one way only, a particular kind of gearing.

clue.text: Locksmith not fully developing corporation

indicators.note: not fully means incomplete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a paunch, and someone developing one is plump

explanation.surface: A company is slowly growing but not quite there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like a firm but means a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Chubb is a long-established British lock and safe maker, founded by locksmiths.

clue.text: Officer covered by very thin protection

indicators.note: being covered by something puts it inside, wrapped round

parts.note: sheer fabric is very thin and fine
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: An officer dressed in flimsy clothes gets little protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter is a place giving cover, refuge or protection.

clue.text: Very large group of nations — very good to get involved

indicators.note: getting involved means getting inside, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: EC was the European Community
pi, short for pious, means very good

explanation.surface: A huge bloc of countries invites a virtuous member to join.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic means vast in scale, as an epic journey is.

clue.text: Film boss to urge variety of cue, right?

parts.note: to prod someone is to urge them on

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different form of it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film boss presses for different cues to be used on set.
explanation.definitionFit: A film producer is the executive who controls a movie's finance and running.

clue.text: Adjust beer container to hold brewed tea? On the contrary

indicators.note: with the contrary twist the brewed tea holds the container rather than the reverse
this flips the clue's stated arrangement, so the tea goes round the container
brewing changes the state of something, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for beer

explanation.surface: A recipe suggests slipping tea into a beer barrel, a strange brewing experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' makes ATE from TEA; 'On the contrary' reverses 'to hold', so ATE holds TUN.
explanation.definitionFit: To attune an instrument or a mind is to bring it into harmony, to adjust it.

clue.text: Buildings disseminating ancestry to us?

indicators.note: disseminating means scattering widely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Family homes spread our lineage down the generations.
explanation.definitionFit: Country seats are stately houses of landed families, grand buildings in the countryside.

clue.text: One makes routine observation true for each, possibly? Somewhat

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could form something else, a rearrangement

parts.note: somewhat means a bit, as in 'a bit tired'

explanation.surface: A pedant notes that something holds true for each case, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges TRUE FOR EACH into the first eleven letters; the definition reads 'observation' as observing a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone set in their ways observes, keeps to, a routine without fail.

clue.text: Isn't involved in the most significant claim

indicators.note: being involved in something puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: main means chief, most significant
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: Someone denies taking part in the central assertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a view is to insist on it, to assert it as true.

clue.text: Row in stadium about good competitor

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: stadium seating rises in tiers, rows above rows

explanation.surface: A fine sportsman is seated somewhere in the stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger is a fierce competitor, a ruthless rival in sport or business.

clue.text: Understood about upset party getting close to making sort of farewell?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the rest

parts.note: got means understood, as in 'I got it'

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns something over, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a do is a party
nigh means close, near

explanation.surface: A guest grasps that the upset party is winding down and says goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the party word into OD; the question mark flags that this is one particular way of saying farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodnight is said when parting in the evening, a particular kind of goodbye.

clue.text: Protection a European's given to soldiers from another continent

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers, from across the Atlantic

explanation.surface: A European enjoys protection from foreign troops stationed in their country.
explanation.definitionFit: To act under the aegis of someone is to have their shield, their protection.

clue.text: Liqueur is filling a requirement

indicators.note: filling something means going inside it

parts.note: a need is a requirement

explanation.surface: A drink is just what's needed.
explanation.walkthrough: IS goes inside the combined ANEED, after its first N.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed is the flavour of liqueurs such as anisette and ouzo, used here for the drink itself.

clue.text: Performer completely at sea about Rossini's finale

parts.note: so means extremely, as in 'so lost'

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: being at sea means bewildered, lost

indicators.note: a finale is the end, so take the last letter

explanation.surface: A musician is utterly lost when it comes to the end of a Rossini work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rossini's finale' looks like the closing of a piece of music but gives only the final letter; 'at sea' is a synonym, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A soloist is a musician who plays or sings a solo, a performer.

clue.text: Opera performance encapsulating a point

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a turn is an act or performance in a show
a dot is a point

explanation.surface: A show is summed up neatly in one key idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance' is a theatrical turn, an act in a show, not the opera's staging.
explanation.definitionFit: Turandot is Puccini's final opera, set in legendary Peking.

clue.text: Unpleasant feeling arising after change of heart

indicators.note: arising in a down clue means going up, so the letters read backwards
the central letter of the word is changed for another

parts.note: an emotion is a feeling

explanation.surface: A bad mood emerges once someone changes their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of EMOTION is T; changing it to S gives EMOSION, which 'arising' turns over.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or disgusting, especially of smells.

clue.text: Following ethical principles, A Lincoln arranged systematic knowledge

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: science is knowledge organised by system and method

explanation.surface: Abraham Lincoln, known for principle, set out knowledge in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in all conscience means acting as one's moral sense requires, by honest principles.

clue.text: Statement in court case mostly taking care of Duke making impromptu comment

indicators.note: taking care of someone means keeping them within, so one piece goes inside
mostly means not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an alibi is a defendant's claim to have been elsewhere

explanation.surface: A duke's lawyer offers an unplanned remark during a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: ALIBI loses its last letter, then D goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: An ad lib is something said on the spur of the moment, unscripted.

clue.text: Topless lingerie item giving you a turn

indicators.note: topless in a down clue means losing the top, the first letter

parts.note: a teddy is a one-piece undergarment

explanation.surface: A glimpse of someone in skimpy underwear gives you a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving you a turn' sounds like a fright, but 'turn' is a swirling motion.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirl of water or air, a circular turn against the current.

clue.text: City hideaway serving up cake

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London, the financial district
a lair is an animal's den, a hideaway

explanation.surface: A café hidden away in the City serves pastries.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry filled with cream and iced with chocolate.

clue.text: Futile embracing female when cornered by wild religious follower

indicators.note: being cornered means being hemmed in, so this goes inside the other piece

parts.note: mad means wild, uncontrolled

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a no-go is something useless or futile, as in 'it's no go'

explanation.surface: A frenzied zealot is caught hugging a woman, a fruitless pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions nest: the female inside 'futile' gives NOFGO, which 'cornered by' places within 'wild'.
explanation.definitionFit: A man of God is a clergyman or holy person, devoted to religion.

clue.text: Not up for pushing back origins of this extreme argument

indicators.note: pushing something back sends it the other way, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: abed means in bed, not yet up

indicators.note: origins are the beginnings, so take the first letters

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to back a radical case, pushing back hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A debate is a formal argument between opposing sides.

clue.text: Claim skill keeps ship to course, ultimately

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so pieces go within

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of persuasion
SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the last letter

explanation.surface: A sailor boasts of the skill that keeps a ship on course.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something is to state it firmly, to claim it as true.
